memorymappedfile-large-random-access.title: Use MemoryMappedFile for suitable large random-access data
memorymappedfile-large-random-access.short: Map file regions when access patterns benefit from virtual memory
memorymappedfile-large-random-access.summary: MemoryMappedFile exposes file contents through mapped views, which can suit large files and shared or random-access workloads without manually reading the whole file into one managed buffer.
memorymappedfile-large-random-access.why: Mapping is not automatically faster than ordinary I/O; view size, access locality, address-space pressure, and platform behavior still matter.
memorymappedfile-large-random-access.tips: Measure against RandomAccess or buffered streams with realistic access patterns and keep view lifetimes bounded.

periodictimer-cancellable-background-loo.title: Build cancellable asynchronous loops with PeriodicTimer
periodictimer-cancellable-background-loo.short: Wait for ticks without blocking a thread
periodictimer-cancellable-background-loo.summary: PeriodicTimer provides an awaitable tick source that fits asynchronous background loops and cancellation.
periodictimer-cancellable-background-loo.why: Thread.Sleep blocks a worker, while ad-hoc delay loops can make cancellation and timer ownership less explicit.
periodictimer-cancellable-background-loo.tips: Dispose the timer, pass the stopping token through the loop, and decide deliberately whether overlapping work is allowed.

exceptiondispatchinfo-preserve-stack.title: Preserve exception dispatch information across boundaries
exceptiondispatchinfo-preserve-stack.short: Re-throw captured failures without replacing their original stack context
exceptiondispatchinfo-preserve-stack.summary: ExceptionDispatchInfo captures an exception together with dispatch state so infrastructure code can propagate it later while retaining useful origin information.
exceptiondispatchinfo-preserve-stack.why: Throwing an exception object again from another location can make diagnostics point primarily at the rethrow site.
exceptiondispatchinfo-preserve-stack.tips: Prefer normal throw; inside the same catch block, and use ExceptionDispatchInfo when an exception must cross an execution boundary.

encoding-decoder-stream-boundaries.title: Decode text correctly across buffer boundaries
encoding-decoder-stream-boundaries.short: A byte buffer can end in the middle of a multi-byte character
encoding-decoder-stream-boundaries.summary: Encoding.Decoder preserves decoding state between chunks, allowing streamed UTF-8 and other variable-width encodings to span read boundaries safely.
encoding-decoder-stream-boundaries.why: Decoding each byte chunk independently can replace or corrupt a character whose encoded bytes are split between chunks.
encoding-decoder-stream-boundaries.tips: Reuse one decoder for the logical stream and flush it only when the final bytes have arrived.

interlocked-shared-counter-state.title: Use Interlocked for small atomic shared-state operations
interlocked-shared-counter-state.short: Avoid a lock when the operation is truly a supported atomic update
interlocked-shared-counter-state.summary: Interlocked provides atomic increments, exchanges, and compare-exchange operations for small pieces of shared state.
interlocked-shared-counter-state.why: A plain read-modify-write such as counter++ can lose updates under concurrency, while a lock may be unnecessary for a simple counter.
interlocked-shared-counter-state.tips: Do not stretch Interlocked into a substitute for synchronization of multi-field invariants; use clearer locking when state changes must move together.

http-response-streaming-headers-read.title: Stream large HTTP responses after headers arrive
http-response-streaming-headers-read.short: Avoid buffering an entire response before processing its body
http-response-streaming-headers-read.summary: HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead lets GetAsync complete after response headers so the body can be consumed incrementally as a stream.
http-response-streaming-headers-read.why: Default buffering can increase memory use and delay processing for large downloads or long-lived response bodies.
http-response-streaming-headers-read.tips: Dispose the response and stream, enforce size and time limits, and propagate cancellation while consuming the body.

aspnet-request-timeout-cancellation.title: Treat ASP.NET Core request timeouts as cooperative cancellation
aspnet-request-timeout-cancellation.short: A timeout signal only helps work that observes cancellation
aspnet-request-timeout-cancellation.summary: Request timeout middleware and RequestAborted provide cancellation signals that application and downstream asynchronous operations should propagate.
aspnet-request-timeout-cancellation.why: A timed-out HTTP request can still leave database, network, or CPU work running if the operation ignores cancellation.
aspnet-request-timeout-cancellation.tips: Pass request cancellation into supported APIs and distinguish client disconnects and timeout cancellation from genuine server faults.

metadata-load-context-inspection.title: Inspect assemblies without executing them with MetadataLoadContext
metadata-load-context-inspection.short: Load metadata for tooling in an isolated reflection-only model
metadata-load-context-inspection.summary: MetadataLoadContext lets tools inspect types and members from assembly files without loading those assemblies for normal execution in the application context.
metadata-load-context-inspection.why: Build tools, analyzers, and plugin inspectors often need metadata but should not execute target assembly initialization or bind it into the main load context.
metadata-load-context-inspection.tips: Supply a resolver containing required framework and dependency assemblies and do not mix reflected Type objects with runtime types casually.

unity-burst-managed-boundaries.title: Design Unity Burst jobs around unmanaged data boundaries
unity-burst-managed-boundaries.short: Burst-compiled hot paths cannot freely use ordinary managed objects
unity-burst-managed-boundaries.summary: Burst and the Job System work best with blittable or unmanaged-style data such as NativeArray rather than object graphs, delegates, and managed allocation.
unity-burst-managed-boundaries.why: Managed references and unsupported runtime features can prevent Burst compilation or force work back outside the optimized job path.
unity-burst-managed-boundaries.tips: Keep managed orchestration outside jobs, move compact data into native containers, and verify Burst compilation and timings in the Profiler.

fire-and-forget-task-lifetime.title: Do not lose ownership of important asynchronous work
fire-and-forget-task-lifetime.short: Fire-and-forget tasks need an explicit lifetime and failure policy
fire-and-forget-task-lifetime.summary: Discarding a Task disconnects its completion, exception, and cancellation from the caller unless another component deliberately owns and observes it.
fire-and-forget-task-lifetime.why: Work can outlive request or object state, failures can become difficult to observe, and shutdown can abandon pending operations.
fire-and-forget-task-lifetime.tips: Await important work; for true background work, hand it to a supervised queue or service that owns cancellation, logging, and shutdown.
